summary:
Diyarbakır is the largest city of south-east Türkiye and stands under the national legal framework applying throughout the country. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct 'contrary to biological sex' with up to three years in prison, and would allow charges against anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony, carrying up to four years.

The same draft would, under civil-code article 40, raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 and impose a permanent-infertility mandate; providers would face fines and up to seven years' imprisonment, patients up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected, and Human Rights Watch has called for the package's withdrawal. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.

The source records no Diyarbakır-specific enforcement, incidents or policing practice; the exposure a trans visitor faces in the city is the national framework above.
tangentialFactors: The draft provisions sit within a broader pattern Human Rights Watch and Kaos GL document nationally, including the 313 violations recorded in the Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 and the six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence that year, three classified as hate killings, with transgender individuals disproportionately affected. Diyarbakır's own record on these counts is not separately sourced.
localsOnly: Residents of Diyarbakır face the same draft provisions as visitors: the proposed criminalisation of conduct 'contrary to biological sex' under penal-code article 225, charges for participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies, and, under civil-code article 40, a rise in the minimum age for gender-affirming care to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate. Providers would face fines and up to seven years, patients up to three years. No province-specific enforcement or incidents are recorded in the source.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since Human Rights Watch's 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

No Diyarbakır-specific enforcement data, incident records or policing practice appear in the inventory; the city's position is carried entirely by the national framework.
